title: What Does a Sparse Autoencoder Feature Do? A Weight-Based Account
claim: Activation-based explanations describe where a component fires but not what it does; weight-based accounts reveal its computational effect.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side; left activation example card, right feature-token list
description: Two panels. Panel (a) is a rounded card for Gemma-2-9B layer 35, feature 11433. It shows three text snippets with tokens highlighted in blue, and the strongest activations are boxed with numeric values such as 121.24. Below the snippets is a gray 'Activation-based explanation' header with a frowning emoji. Under it is a GPT-4o-mini summary: 'scientific terminology and statistical data related to genetic research'. A green 'Weight-based' line follows, reading 'predict next token "among"', with a target emoji. Panel (b) is titled Gemma-2-9B Layer 27. It lists seven features. Each has L, C and E scores on the right and a row of boxed predicted tokens, such as freezer/refrigeration/ice or trust/trustworthy. Light blue token chips and boxed score ranges carry the contrast. The eye goes first to the highlighted tokens on the left.
caption: Two views of SAE features. (a) An activation-based explanation read off the feature’s top-activating contexts: tokens where the feature fires are highlighted and the highest activations are boxed, and GPT-4o-mini summarizes the co-occurring text. The summary does not specify what changes in the model’s computation when the feature is suppressed. (b) A uniform sample of features that pass all three weight-based metrics in Section 4 on Gemma-2-9B at layer 27, shown with their top-10 predicted tokens. “L” is Levenshtein similarity, “C” is cosine similarity, and “E” is top-100 entropy; boxed scores correspond to the range of displayed tokens.
abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) have emerged as a powerful technique for decomposing language model representations into interpretable features. Current interpretation pipelines infer feature semantics from activation patterns, implicitly assuming every feature has a semantic explanation while overlooking the computational roles features inherit from the SAE training objective. We introduce a weight-based interpretation framework that requires no activation data and grounds claims causally through targeted feature-ablation interventions. Across Gemma-2 and Llama-3.1, three depth-dependent signatures show that SAE features inherit the base model's geometry: semantic features form a U-shape under tied embeddings but bifurcate when untied, attention participation peaks mid-layer, and the two roles couple oppositely for input- vs. output-oriented features. This weight-based view supplies the causal half missing from activation-based interpretability.
